articles.title: Molten Metal
articles.summary: Burnt orange metal with fine diagonal scratches and bright sparkle, like brushed copper catching light. A warm burnt-orange metallic with gentle dark mottling; reads as brushed copper, mid-dark and rich, with the scratches almost gone.
articles.what: Up close: Burnt-orange and copper surface with a fine diagonal twill grain, soft dark-brown and bright orange patches about 100-150px wide, and a few long hair-thin bright scratch lines crossing at angles. No cells or shapes, just metal with grain and a handful of scratches. From a distance: A warm burnt-orange metallic with gentle dark mottling; reads as brushed copper, mid-dark and rich, with the scratches almost gone. Measured spec (average): metal 166, roughness 87, coat 91. Shine: satin. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: stock car, gt / sports car, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Molten Metal" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: grain and mottling suit big panels
A good base under numbers, stripes and sponsor graphics
Moderate texture, no big shapes, so white or black numbers read cleanly; thin scratches are too fine to bother them.
Fine metal flake or glitter: adds to the sparkle that is already there but stays quiet
Pairs well with: black, dark grey, chrome, deep red.
pitfalls: Not a lava or magma look: no glowing veins or cells
Not a flat orange paint: grain, mottling and scratches are visible
Avoid: small numbers over the scratch texture, next to other sparkle finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 166 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 87 (satin gloss), clearcoat 91 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over the scratch texture, next to other sparkle finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine metal flake or glitter: adds to the sparkle that is already there but stays quiet; a light carbon or weave only if kept faint
Patterns to avoid: large bold patterns, camo and flames: they bury the delicate grain
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat variation: brings up the copper depth; brushed or fine grain spec following the diagonal
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
